name: Construction
pullQuote: Civic infrastructure answers to the people who use it thirty years from now.
overview: Construction is the group's oldest line of work and the one that set its habits. Civic building imposes a discipline commercial work does not always demand — the client is ultimately the public, and the public keeps the building far longer than anyone involved in putting it up. That changes what counts as a good decision on site.

The business covers structures intended to stay in service for generations rather than lease cycles. Much of the judgement sits in specification: choosing the material that will still be serviceable when the people who chose it are gone, rather than the one that surveys best on completion.

approach.heading: Building for the second generation
body: Specification is written for the second generation of a structure's users. That means favouring materials and details that can be maintained with ordinary skill and ordinary parts, because a building that needs a specialist to keep working will eventually stop working.

Sequencing matters as much as selection. Civic sites are usually occupied, adjacent to something in use, or both, so the programme is planned around keeping the surroundings functioning rather than around the shortest path to handover.

capabilities.title: Civic and institutional
capabilities.description: Buildings held in public use, planned around long service rather than short cycles.

capabilities.title: Refurbishment

capabilities.title: Quality assurance
capabilities.description: Checking work against the specification while it can still be corrected.
